strengths: The bold sans title and item names pair with prominent serif start times to give the component a distinct, task-specific type voice. The tracked uppercase text serves metadata rather than forming a generic editorial opening.
The reading path reaches the first agenda item quickly on desktop and phone. Item names, start times, durations, and reset remain easy to locate.

At 320px, names wrap without losing their relationship to times and durations. The drag frame distinguishes the held item and proposed position; the reordered frame shows the new times and a clear confirmation.
limits: The captures show individual states, so they cannot establish motion quality, keyboard behavior, or whether the times remain stable throughout a drag.

strengths: The agenda makes the task clear: move items to update their start times. Reset and keyboard guidance are visible.
The default and reordered captures preserve item durations and show consistent start times; the programme still ends at 18:50. The reordered state confirms the move locally.
The drag capture distinguishes the held item and prospective slot while showing the nearby item move to make room.
The 390px and 320px layouts remain readable, with titles wrapping without collisions. The time-led hierarchy suits an event running order.
limits: Static captures cannot verify touch or keyboard operation, focus behavior, cancelled drags, rapid reversal, resize behavior, or reduced motion.
The referenced motion playback was not supplied, so its relationship to this design cannot be judged.
